attacks.claim: Wire-photo coverage for new sizes and formats rests on an internal photo-desk confirmation that is not attached and whose licence terms are not quoted. Agency licences often restrict derivative works, so the legal basis for creating and publishing about 310k new derivatives is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Extra sizes and formats of the same licensed image for the same display use are covered by the current licences (photo desk confirmation on WEB-778, Oct 19)."

attacks.claim: Stripping all metadata from every output removes IPTC/XMP credit, copyright and usage-terms fields. Licensed wire and agency photos often require these, and the markup renders only alt text, so the plan may breach attribution obligations. Preserving or re-rendering credits is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: "all metadata is stripped (`strip=True`)... assert none of it survives in any output."

attacks.claim: The takedown path is not failure-aware. S3 key deletion and the wildcard CloudFront invalidation run as separate steps with no described partial-failure handling, retry, completion check, or alert. A legal takedown can be left half-applied, with derivatives deleted but cached HTML or CDN objects still served.
attacks.evidence: "It is extended to delete every key under the image's `<id>-` prefix and invalidate `/media/YYYY/MM/<id>-*`." and "Test: purge an image with a full responsive set; assert zero remaining keys and one wildcard invalidation."

attacks.claim: The main worker hardening control, VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1, is asserted for libvips 8.14 from Debian 12 with no citation or test showing that this version honours it. If the control is absent or a no-op, untrusted-input protection for the upload pipeline is not in place.
attacks.evidence: "libvips 8.14 from the Debian 12 package (LGPL-2.1, dynamically linked...)" and "workers run with `VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1`." No verification is cited.

attacks.claim: The backfill schedule has about 0.3 h of headroom in a 10 h window, based on a single c6i.xlarge prototype with no retry or failure allowance. Nothing tracks how many images still lack has_responsive_set or alerts on backlog, so a shortfall would leave articles silently on plain .
attacks.evidence: "0.9 s per image for the full set (prototype, c6i.xlarge). Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers ≈ 9.7 h, run over two nights (01:00–06:00)"

attacks.claim: The promise that publishing is never delayed has no isolation mechanism. The low-priority queue runs on the same two worker nodes as publishing, with no separate pool, resource limits, or routing check. Memory-heavy libvips jobs on 40-megapixel inputs can hold slots and delay publishing.
attacks.evidence: "run over two nights (01:00–06:00) on a separate low-priority Celery queue, so publishing tasks are never delayed." with "Two existing worker nodes × 4 workers"

attacks.claim: Takedown does not say whether has_responsive_set is cleared. If it stays true, articles can keep emitting <picture> sources that point at deleted keys, and the 60 s CDN HTML cache prolongs this. The existing img src is also removed, so this is partly the intended effect, but the page state is not defined.
attacks.evidence: "`<picture>` is rendered only when `image.has_responsive_set` is true (set by the task)." and "HTML cache TTL at the CDN is 60 s."

attacks.claim: The success target of p75 mobile LCP ≤ 2.5 s is not reached by the plan's own prototype, which measured 2.6 s on 50 articles with 3 runs each. The target is asserted without evidence that full rollout will reach it.
attacks.evidence: "WebPageTest (Moto G Power, 4G, 3 runs per article): p75 LCP 3.9 s → 2.6 s." versus "CrUX p75 mobile LCP on article pages ≤ 2.5 s within 6 weeks of 100%."

attacks.claim: Visual quality at AVIF q50 and WebP q75 for news photography is unvalidated. The prototype reports only byte sizes, and the rollout compares LCP and CLS, not image quality, yet these settings reach 100% of articles.
attacks.evidence: "AVIF (q 50) and WebP (q 75) at 480/800/1200/1600 px" versus "800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB" (size only).

attacks.claim: The JPEG srcset stops at 1200 px while AVIF and WebP go to 1600 px. Browsers that fall back to JPEG on high-DPR screens cannot pick 1600 px, so the fallback will look softer than the modern formats.
attacks.evidence: "an `` with the JPEG `srcset`; `src` is the existing 1600 px JPEG" with JPEG derivatives at "480/800/1200 px" versus "480/800/1200/1600 px" for AVIF and WebP

attacks.claim: width and height come from 'stored dimensions', which may be those of the original rather than the applied crop. A mismatched aspect ratio would undermine the CLS budget, which is only 0.01 above the 0.04 baseline.
attacks.evidence: "gains `width`/`height` from stored dimensions to prevent layout shift" and "No CLS regression: p75 ≤ 0.05 (today 0.04)."

attacks.claim: The ~340 KB per-image storage estimate is inconsistent with the plan's prototype figures. The 800 px AVIF and WebP alone total 149 KB, and the 1200 and 1600 px variants are larger, so the full new set is likely several times 340 KB.
attacks.evidence: "~340 KB of new derivatives per image → ~105 GB for the backfill" alongside "800 px AVIF median 61 KB, WebP 88 KB"

attacks.claim: The ~$1,000/month CloudFront saving is projected from 800 px prototype byte counts on one device profile. High-DPR devices fetch 1200 or 1600 px, which are much larger, so the saving is likely overstated.
attacks.evidence: "projected ~9 TB by applying the prototype's byte savings to September's traffic mix, ≈ $1,000/month less. This is an estimate"
